one_month_reasoning: In-window events: Virginia SCC local public hearings on the Dominion merger Oct 7 (Newport News) and Oct 9 (Fairfax) - public comment, not rulings, so low price impact; September jobs and CPI prints in early/mid October; Q3 2026 earnings, date unconfirmed by NEE IR (TipRanks estimates Oct 22, Q3 2025 was Oct 28) but inside the window either way; and the Oct 28 FOMC. Correcting round 1: after the cooler August PCE on Sep 30 (+0.2% m/m vs 0.3%), swaps price only ~36% odds of an October hike (from >70%), so the FOMC is now closer to a two-sided event than a priced-in negative, and the Sep 30 close already reflects that relief. NEE has beaten adjusted EPS recently and targets the high end of $3.92-4.02, so earnings lean mildly positive, offset by the Sep 29 Oklahoma Uri liability headline and a still-high 10-year (5.24% Sep 28). Net: near-symmetric lognormal centred ~$76.1 (tiny upward tilt from earnings and the reduced hike odds), sigma ~6.5% (21%/3.5 plus a little for earnings and FOMC), slightly fattened tails.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E on NTM EPS at Sep-2027 ($4.58 = 0.25 x 2027E $4.33 + 0.75 x 2028E $4.67, x 18x = $82.4) at 60% and dividend-yield method (2027 run-rate DPS $2.64 / 3.25% = $81.2) at 40%, giving ~$82 twelve months out. The $4.83B NEE-paid regulatory break fee (~$2.30/share) is carried in the bear scenario and ladder rather than the fair value.

Today's yield $2.49 / $75.9 = 3.28%, held roughly flat: 10y at a 19-year high argues against re-rating back to the ~2.5-2.8% yields of 2025-mid 2026, but ~36% October hike odds post-PCE reduce the case for further compression

bear.story: Yields push toward 5.5-6% as hikes resume; utilities de-rate toward the 2023 trough (~14-15x on ~$4.3-4.6 = $62-66), and the Virginia SCC/NCUC/SC PSC signal rejection or burdensome conditions, which the market prices as ~$2.30/share of NEE-paid regulatory break fee ($4.83B) on top of lost growth credit; plus Oklahoma Uri damages headlines. Net ~$60.

base.story: EPS compounds ~8% (NTM ~$4.58 at horizon), rates plateau near current levels, merger proceeds on a delayed but workable timetable (SCC ruling Jan-Mar 2027 with concessions, close late 2027); multiple ~17.5-18x gives ~$80-82 plus ~3.3% dividend.

bull.story: Rates peak and ease in 2027 (October hike odds already fell to ~36%), data-center load and the 35 GW backlog drive beats, Dominion approvals arrive with manageable conditions and 9%+ combined growth is credited; multiple returns to ~21-21.5x NTM $4.58, back near the $98.75 May 2026 high.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$58 (~12.7x NTM $4.58, under the regulated-utility median and the 2023 rate-shock trough multiple) the market would be pricing something fundamental: a cut to the 8%+ EPS CAGR, a credit/rating problem funding ~$107B net debt plus merger and capex at 5%+ rates, or a regulatory breakdown of the Dominion deal. A deal rejection alone costs ~$2.30/share (the NEE-paid $4.83B fee) plus some de-rating, which should take the stock to the low/mid $60s, not below $58, unless combined with a growth reset.

reasoning: Base-rate lane, round 2. Supervisor corrections adopted: (1) NTM EPS at the horizon is ~$4.58, not full-year 2028 $4.67, trimming the P/E leg to $82.4 at an unchanged 18x (~today's 17.9x NTM); (2) the dividend is $0.6232/qtr ($2.49), so the Sep-2027 run-rate is $2.64 and the yield leg rises to $81.2 at 3.25% (vs a timing-mismatched $82 before); blended FV ~$82 (from $83). (3) Deal failure is not neutral: NEE pays Dominion $4.83B (~$2.30/share) on regulatory termination (confirmed in the 424B3), so I moved this from 'mildly positive' into the bear case. Base rate update: HECO (2016) and Oncor (2017) were outright failures, but broader US utility M&A history shows initial rejections are often cured by restructuring or settlements (Great Plains-Westar rejected 2017, approved 2018; Exelon-Pepco rejected by DC 2015, approved 2016), so I still put ultimate approval at ~75-80%, with delay risk (AG clock motion could push the SCC deadline to March 2027). Expected break-fee drag ~P(fail within horizon ~12%) x $2.30 = ~$0.30, small. (4) October hike odds fell from ~67% to ~36% after the Sep 30 PCE, a modest positive already in the close; the 10y is still 5.24%. (5) Oklahoma Uri ruling is unquantified headline risk (~$0.50/share per $1B). Distribution: 2023 base rate shows NEE can fall ~40% in a rate shock and rebound 60%+ once yields peak, so tails stay fat. I keep a 12-month median ~$79 (below FV because rate momentum is negative; above spot on ~8% EPS growth and a near-trough multiple), lognormal sigma ~0.24 with slightly fat tails; P(>=76) nudged to 0.57 from 0.56 as easing hike odds offset the break-fee correction, upper strikes trimmed slightly for the NTM EPS fix. I did not copy the supervisor's 0.59 at K=76: with the 10y at a 19-year high and hiking not ruled out, I see a bit more downside path than the forecaster mean. Research kept tight (4 new searches); Bloomberg content from search snippet.
